application.cover_letter_markdown:
Oulu keeps coming up when I think about where I want to be working next. The concentration of RF and photonics companies, the Suvanto wireless labs, the university’s radar research group, the space-systems supply chain — it is unusually dense for a mid-sized city, and it is the reason this posting caught my eye before anything in the job description itself.

I have been at Sumuvire Wireless since early 2022, working on signal processing for communications and radar receivers. Most of my time has gone into receiver signal chains — real-time embedded firmware, beamforming algorithms for phased arrays, RF calibration and characterisation, and the Python tooling that ties the test infrastructure together. The specific projects are on my CV so I will not repeat them here, but the short version is that I have done hands-on signal processing at every stage from algorithm design to production firmware to anechoic chamber measurements, and I have shipped work that is running in deployed hardware.

There is a gap in my timeline that I should address. I took a year off in 2024–25 — a sabbatical I had been planning for a while, mostly travel and reading. I came back to the same team at Sumuvire in October 2025 and picked up where I left off without difficulty. I am not going to dress it up as a strategic career move; it was personal. But I also do not think it cost me anything technically, and the distance was useful in clarifying what kind of work I want to keep doing and where I want to do it.

Kaikuvaara’s focus on remote-sensing instruments — SAR payloads, scatterometers, ground-segment signal processing — sits at the intersection of what I have been doing and what I want to do next. I have some familiarity with Kalman filtering and estimation theory, which I understand is relevant to the tracking and calibration problems that come with spaceborne and airborne instruments. The opportunity to work on instruments that actually fly, from a team based in Oulu, is the most interesting position I have come across since moving to Finland.

I visited Oulu for a calibration campaign at Suvanto in 2023 and stayed a few extra days because I liked the place. The engineering community there is small enough that people working on adjacent problems actually run into each other — that does not happen in Helsinki, where the tech scene is broader but more fragmented. For someone who wants to stay in Finland and keep doing deep-tech signal processing rather than drifting into process and management, Oulu is the right city. I would welcome the chance to be part of that community rather than visiting it occasionally.

Stefan Bianchi

I’ve been following Kaikuvaara’s work in spaceborne remote-sensing instruments for a while now. When your involvement in the Aurelia follow-on payload study was reported last year, that was when I decided I wanted to work there rather than just admire the engineering from a distance. The kind of mission-critical instrument work your team does — building signal chains that have to work on a platform you cannot service after launch — is exactly what I want to be doing next.

Some context on my background. I studied physics at the Merihaka University, graduating in 2018 with a thesis on microwave propagation modelling for layered atmospheric structures. That work was essentially the physics behind radar remote-sensing retrievals: wave-matter interaction, multiple-scattering corrections, and the statistical framework for inverting backscatter measurements into geophysical parameters. It gave me a grounding in electromagnetic theory and statistical signal processing that I have relied on every working day since.

At Kajanti Avionics, most of my signal-processing work has been in the RF tracking and measurement domain, but the project I think translates most directly to Kaikuvaara is a phased-array beamforming system I built for a ground-based direction-finding receiver. It was an 8-element circular array where I designed the null-steering algorithm, computed the array manifold from measured element patterns, and validated the beam output against live field data. That was hands-on array signal processing from geometry through to steering vectors, and it is the piece of my experience I expect you would find most relevant.

I should also mention the embedded side. Before the career break I took in 2021, I wrote the C firmware for a real-time spectral channeliser running on a TI C6678 DSP — DMA scheduling, fixed-point FFT pipeline, interrupt handling. It was a demanding platform under tight timing constraints, and the firmware shipped in the end product. I don’t have years of embedded experience beyond that project, but it was real production code running on real hardware.

The break itself, 2021–22, was for retraining in applied statistics and computational methods — partly self-directed study, partly short university courses. It sharpened skills I use regularly now and I came back to the same team feeling technically stronger for it, not weaker.

All technical work at Kajanti — documentation, code review, design reports, customer-facing deliverables — is conducted in English. I have never worked in another language professionally and am fully comfortable operating in an English-only technical environment.

I am looking specifically at Oulu for this move. Partly because of Kaikuvaara, and partly because the city’s RF and photonics ecosystem feels like the right place to build a career in instrument-level signal processing. I’m ready to relocate and would welcome the chance to discuss the role.

Kari Salo

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Since joining Sumuvire Wireless three years ago, my work has been almost entirely in the RF test lab — characterising front-end modules, measuring antenna patterns, running calibration campaigns on new hardware. It is detailed, hands-on work that I find genuinely satisfying, but the natural question after three years of it is whether I want to stay in test and measurement for the rest of my career or move toward something broader. This posting is my answer to that question.

I came into RF work from an unusual angle. My master’s at SIT Bombay was in biomedical engineering, which does not sound connected at first, but a significant part of what I studied — sensor characterisation, noise modelling, measurement uncertainty analysis — turns out to be directly transferable to RF test work. When I moved to Finland and started at Sumuvire, I picked up the domain-specific pieces quickly because the underlying measurement principles were already familiar. The learning curve was steep but not as steep as it might have been.

What I’ve built in three years is a solid working knowledge of RF characterisation: I’ve measured dozens of front-end modules across Sumuvire’s product range, run antenna pattern campaigns in both near-field and far-field configurations, and been responsible for the calibration integrity of the department’s main test bench. I know the instruments well, I understand the pitfalls of real-world RF measurement, and I can produce a characterisation report that an engineer can use without having to reinterpret my data.

What I do not yet have is experience on the design and algorithm side — working out the signal-processing chains rather than testing the hardware they run on. That is what I am looking for in this role. Kaikuvaara’s work in remote-sensing instruments is the kind of technically deep environment where I believe the transition from measurement into design makes sense, because measurement knowledge does not stop being useful once you cross into design — it feeds into a different stage of the same system.

I am based in Helsinki and have been considering Oulu for some time. I am a Finnish citizen and would relocate for the right position.

I’d be glad to discuss my background in more detail.

Marika Nieminen

I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss whether there is a fit.

Paivi Kinnunen

I find that combination of constraint and consequence genuinely appealing, and it is not a dynamic that exists in the commercial receiver products I work on today.

application.cover_letter_markdown:
I saw the Senior Signal Processing Engineer posting while looking at engineering roles across the Nordic region, and I want to be straightforward: my background is in mechanical engineering, not signal processing. I am applying anyway because the work sounds genuinely interesting to me and because I have reached a point in my career where I am seriously considering a change of field.

I have spent fourteen years designing HVAC systems at Hedlund Klimat here in Gothenburg. The work is technical and detailed — sizing ductwork for large commercial buildings involves thermal modelling, fluid dynamics calculations, compliance with a thicket of building regulations, and constant coordination with other engineering disciplines. I have become good at it, but I have also largely exhausted what the field can teach me. The problems repeat, the tools are mature, and the engineering challenge has plateaued.

What caught my attention about this particular posting is the Oulu region. I have read about the concentration of RF and photonics companies there, the links to the space industry, and the kind of instrument engineering that happens in a compact technical community where people working on related problems actually know each other. It is a very different world from Gothenburg’s automotive-and-heavy-industry engineering scene, and I find the idea of being part of something like that genuinely appealing even though I know I would be arriving with a very different skill set.

I do not have experience in signal processing, RF engineering, embedded software, or the other technical areas listed in the posting. I want to be clear about that rather than attempt to repackage mechanical engineering experience as something it is not. What I do have is fourteen years of disciplined engineering practice: working within tight physical and regulatory constraints, reading and interpreting complex technical specifications, delivering to deadlines, and picking up new technical domains when a project calls for it. I also have a solid engineering education from Gotaalv, even if it was in the wrong discipline for this role.

If there is scope for someone with a general engineering background to contribute to your team — whether in this role or in another capacity where mechanical and systems engineering would be more directly applicable — I would genuinely like to hear about it. If the gap is too large, I understand that completely. I thought it was worth writing regardless.

Wei Chen

application.cover_letter_markdown:
What draws me to this role is the instrument work itself. I have spent my career at Kajanti Avionics doing signal processing for ground-based radar, and while it has been technically rewarding work, the step I want to take next is into remote-sensing instruments — systems where the signal chain starts at a payload antenna and the data products serve a purpose beyond a radar operator’s display.

Kaikuvaara builds exactly that. SAR payloads, scatterometers, ground-segment signal processors — it is the same signal-processing discipline I have been practising for most of my career, applied to a different and more interesting class of problem. The DSP fundamentals are the same, the RF front-end design challenges are familiar, and the difference is the platform and the mission. I want that difference.

Oulu is part of the decision. I have been in Helsinki for almost my entire working life, and the engineering community here is broad rather than deep in any one area. Oulu’s wireless and photonics cluster — the university, Suvanto, the instrument and space-systems companies concentrated within a few kilometres of each other — feels like the kind of environment where someone building signal-processing systems for instruments would find both collaborators and momentum. I have thought about this move for a while and this posting was what prompted me to act on it rather than continue thinking about it.

I will not duplicate my CV here, but the summary is that I have extensive hands-on experience across the areas your posting describes: phased-array beamforming, embedded firmware, production software, and RF measurement at subsystem and component level. I have been doing this work long enough that I am confident in my ability to contribute from day one in a new environment.

I would be glad to discuss the role and what your team is looking for in more detail.

Meera Adeyemi
